hunks.patch:
@@ -776,3 +776,30 @@ Future entries must include the date, approved rule change or clarification, aff
 - Local evidence passed JavaScript syntax, 27/27 focused Banking/modal/cache tests and the new exact source/CSS regression. The complete non-browser frontend suite passed 1,410/1,412; the same two unrelated failures reproduced on the untouched `e58e567f66ed8108a40e3c3e8388dbe33e0b0361` baseline at 1,409/1,411, proving this change added one passing test and no failure. Publication and a real new-session browser lifecycle remain required before this entry is release-complete.
 - Policy X assessment: compliant. The correction exposes an already-existing pre-Draft user action and changes no selection authority, selected identity, amount, tax/VAT, PAYE/Umbrella rule, recovery/headroom, Draft input, frozen artifact, provider, payment, settlement, remittance or cancellation behaviour.
 
+### 4 October 2026 — isolated thin NEXT Office caller (local source evidence)
+
+- This isolated frontend worktree adds a separate Banking Pay NEXT menu entry and a thin caller for explicit ALL-Work pages, server-owned preparation/review/confirmation, PAYE net intake, original transfer/CSV retrieval and streamed original-instruction advice. It does not boot the retired financial Workbench, claim/drain jobs, calculate money or replace frozen facts with current Timesheet/settings data. Current approval/position rows are factual inputs, not a browser eligibility ruling; a later approval flag remains informational after Draft.
+- Before each mutation, an actor-namespaced session journal saves the exact action bytes and UUIDs. An unknown or malformed receipt pauses conflicting controls; only an explicit identical-request retry is offered. Close and session clear remove the sheet/poller without deleting that journal. Actor changes refuse before network, and NEXT response payloads are neither cloned nor logged even when existing API debug logging is enabled. The existing authentication/session owners otherwise remain unchanged.
+- Local source evidence passed 25/25 focused unit tests and JavaScript syntax checks. Four local Chromium tests used the actual new module with explicitly synthetic closed-contract responses, zero external HTTP requests, hostile labels, bounded factual pages, lost-reply close/resume, actor-session close and reachable mobile Close. The 300-row test proves only factual pagination (100/100/100), not selection/preparation of 300 genuine Timesheets or whole-application performance. Synthetic gross/net/recovery/cash displays do not prove their financial owners.
+- Actual authenticated API/browser joining, normal login, hosted publication, complete Stage 4/5 screens, current-week/future eligibility policy and full Stage 7 remittance configuration/delivery remain separate acceptance. No database, provider, email, deployment, commit or push was performed for this frontend source proof. This entry records the thin caller only and changes no business rule or Policy X authority.
+
+### 5 October 2026 — Candidate-only bank navigation and batch returned-cash facts (local)
+
+- Bank details remain editable only in the existing Candidate owner. The thin NEXT batch-status caller delegates only the exact Candidate UUID, closes its top-layer sheet and preserves its actor journal/frozen run. Reopening retains accepted state. Still-valid exact account/beneficiary/rail verification and confirmation must be reused; changed details require their own approval. This navigation does not itself implement or certify the bank review/issue bridge.
+- A separate closed RETURN_CASH page displays only this run/worker's original returned transfers and maintained cash balances; existing STATUS is unchanged. Posting-incomplete balances remain NULL, not zero or spendable. The caller accepts empty advancing raw windows and follows the server cursor over skipped legs, never accumulates all Candidate history or computes repayment amounts. Status refresh clears the prior return display. Available cash is not bank/payment approval, and no repay/issue control or account-entry form is added before its genuine bank-safety join exists.
+- E136 records actual 38/38 local unit PASS and two actual-module/synthetic-response Chromium PASS with no external HTTP. The latter prove navigation/journal retention/paging/pending copy only, not native money, generic Candidate hydration/edit/save, complete batch-tab UX, return alerts, bank checks, provider execution, hosted installation or full programme closure. No business economics or Policy X changed; returned money stays separate from main earnings and the next ordinary Draft.
+
+### 5 October 2026 — bounded multi-Candidate thin selection and captured detail (local)
+
+- The thin NEXT view can choose another Candidate in the same unsealed run. Accepted global Work page/count receipts remain attached to that run; only the current factual page, unsubmitted choices and Candidate-scoped Case journal are replaced. Any uncertain request or unsealed accepted Case page blocks switching. An exact accepted Case seal is retained before changing Candidate; one decimal-text prior-selected-Case count preserves case-only preparation without fabricating Work or keeping a Candidate-wide history array. Reopening uses the same actor journal and exact unknown bytes.
+- Journal version 2 distinguishes that new scalar from a damaged journal. Only complete older version-1 metadata may adopt an exact zero prior-Candidate count, because that caller could not switch Candidates after creating the run. Existing current-Candidate Case-only counts, sealed state and pending request bytes are unchanged. A version-2 missing/malformed scalar refuses; prior sealed Case choices cannot migrate to another run. The existing public owner still controls initial per-Candidate revision/page, exact replay and sealed-manifest refusal; the browser never invents a later Case revision.
+- Before CSV, each frozen payment line can open paged captured shifts, its exact shift-scoped breaks and used bucket rates. Available contract/channel rates use the captured run-Work ID supplied by the existing revision-comparison reader; a newer-approval flag is informational only. Decimal text, zero, NULL, local/UTC clocks, overnight facts, duration-only breaks and exclusions are retained. Approved quantities/segment amounts are labelled separately from the selected payment difference; no hours-times-rate calculation, blended rate or mutable Timesheet/settings enrichment is introduced. Failed scope changes clear old detail controls even if the previous status read already failed.
+- Local verification passed 50/50 focused unit/caller checks and 15/15 actual-module Chromium tests using controlled contract responses and no external HTTP. The new transport tests call the actual saved frozen-detail and preparation handlers with controlled RAW rows. This proves the caller/presentation boundary, not native SQL money or a DB-to-browser join, whole-application performance, first-300 preparation, login, hosted publication, payment/provider execution or full screens. Existing financial writers, original advice printing, Candidate-only bank editing and returned-cash separation are unchanged. No DB, Docker, deployment, commit or push was performed; Policy X is preserved.
+
+### 6 October 2026 — explicit Office NEXT history caller (local controlled evidence)
+
+- Existing Candidate and genuine Timesheet view modals expose an admin-only `Payment history` action. It opens a read-only child in the existing modal framework; normal record and Banking loads do not fetch history. The backend's existing authenticated admin broker supplies the actual actor, not a browser actor, to the service-only permission-checked history reader on every bounded page. No NEXT activation, preparation, mutation or worker drain is invoked by the history caller.
+- All 52 declared sections remain visible in the manifest. Captured parent/FK links expose their child sections; `Next page` follows the complete scope/parent/context/upper-bound cursor until explicit `End`. Only the current page is retained; there is no automatic all-history scan, aggregate or first-page-only claim. Live keyset pages require an explicit refresh for late commits. Current caches/status, immutable source amounts, frozen target ex/VAT, whole-worker NET and whole-transfer cash stay separately labelled; transfer membership does not invent a Timesheet cash allocation. Exact decimal text and NULL survive; dates retain the established day/month/year presentation and UTC clocks.
+- Local evidence passed seven backend controlled handler/transport checks, seven Office controller/source checks and one actual-asset Chromium test at 390 x 844 with zero external requests. They prove closed field allowlists, authenticated-actor injection, byte limits, cursor/scope binding, two revision pages and nested detail, hostile-label escaping, reachable Close and actor-change/close cleanup. The browser uses explicitly controlled responses and a modal-framework fixture; it does not prove real login, installed SQL execution/query plans, authenticated API-to-SQL joining, the complete production modal framework, deployed UI or complete moved-root financial continuity.
+- Policy X: no financial writer, conversion, price, selected membership, residual/headroom, frozen Draft, provider, settlement, recovery, cancellation or remittance authority changes. Not-yet-implemented moved-root/vector/comparison/general approval attribution is stated as unavailable rather than reconstructed. No database, network, deployment, commit or push was performed for this caller implementation.
+
